newsitem.title: USA: NY physical coffee - spot business still lags.
newsitem.headline: NY physical coffee - spot business still lags.

text.p: The New York physical coffee market remained sluggish this week, with only scattered spot sales, as many processors seemed content to stay on the sidelines and wait for the CSCE September contract to go off the board, traders said.

September's more than 20-cent premium to second-month December discouraged prompt business, they said, although some traders maintained there was still a good amount of roaster price-fixing still to be done against September ahead of its first notice day on August 21.
"It's only three weeks to first notice day and there's still a lot of price-fixing to do," said a trader. "We've been seeing odd fill-ins, but nobody's doing anything in a major way.
"It's quiet, it's still summertime," he added.

Much of the talk this week continued to center on exchange certified coffee stocks. Dealers said a major trade house contested six lots of coffee certified for delivery against the July contract and that two lots failed. The CSCE was unavailable for comment.
Meanwhile, differentials held fairly steady on the week.
Spot Colombian MAMs continued to fetch 23 cents over "C", while Brazilian Santos 4s, also on the spot market, were heard at 14 cents under "C".
Elsewhere, spot prime washed Mexican beans netted one cent under "C" and spot high grown Mexicans garnered two cents over "C", both FOB Laredo.
CSCE September coffee rose 0.45 cent a lb Friday to settle at 184.95. December ended 0.25 cent weaker at 162.30.
